style: grandmother as the logger: formal full sentences, calls him 'my grandson', adds her own worries, signs off 'Nana'

situations.name: Eating solid food at family dinner
situations.feared_outcome: A piece will get stuck in my throat and I won't be able to breathe

behaviors.text: Cuts food into tiny pieces and drinks water after every bite
Won't eat meat or bread; asks for soup or a smoothie instead

accommodations.text: Grandma makes him a separate soft meal

behaviors.text: Refuses to swallow his allergy pill whole

accommodations.text: Grandma crushes the pill into applesauce

situations.name: Eating in front of friends (school lunch, eating out)
situations.feared_outcome: I'll choke in front of everyone and someone will have to do the Heimlich on me

behaviors.text: Started eating pizza at a friend's, felt his throat tighten, left the table for the bathroom and didn't finish
Carries a water bottle everywhere and sips before each bite
Quiet at lunch, pushing food around his tray

monitoring_log.situation: Sunday supper. I made a pot roast, which used to be his favorite.
monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: My grandson cut his meat into very small pieces, smaller than a pea, and took a drink of water after every single bite. He ate perhaps a quarter of what was on his plate. He said he was not hungry.
monitoring_log.parent_response: I did not say anything at the table, as I did not want to embarrass him. Afterward I made him a bowl of tomato soup so he would not go to bed hungry. I worry he is getting thin. - Nana

monitoring_log.situation: His allergy tablet in the morning.
monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Jonah would not swallow the tablet. He held it in his hand for a long while and then said he could not do it.
monitoring_log.parent_response: I crushed it with the back of a spoon and mixed it into applesauce, as I have been doing since the summer. He took it that way. - Nana

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: He asked if he could have a smoothie instead. He did not touch the chicken.
monitoring_log.parent_response: I made him a banana smoothie. I know the doctor said not to make a separate meal, but I could not bear to see him go without. - Nana

monitoring_log.situation: Pizza at his friend Marcus's house after the football game.
monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Marcus's mother told me he took a few bites of pizza and then said his throat felt tight. He went to the bathroom and stayed there quite a while. When he came out he did not eat any more and asked to be picked up early.
monitoring_log.parent_response: I drove over and collected him. In the car I asked whether he wished to talk about it, and he said no. - Nana

monitoring_log.parent_words: Jonah's teacher rang me. She says at lunch he sits with his friends but hardly eats, just moves his food about on the tray and does not say much. I cannot tell whether it is the choking business or whether something else is going on at school. He carries that water bottle everywhere now. I did not know what to say to her. - Nana

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Same as before. Would not take it whole.
monitoring_log.parent_response: Crushed it into the applesauce. - Nana

monitoring_log.situation: Supper with his mother visiting. Spaghetti and meatballs.
monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: He ate the spaghetti after cutting it all up very small and had water between every forkful. Would not have a meatball. His mother asked him why and he got upset and said 'because I could choke and die, okay?'
monitoring_log.parent_response: I told his mother to leave it be. I had a pot of soup on the stove already and gave him a bowl. - Nana

voice_notes.text: hello this is nana um jonahs grandmother i am recording this for the doctor um this evening he wouldnt eat the pork chop again and i made him soup and um and this morning the tablet i put it in the applesauce like always he would not swallow it i suppose it was an eight at supper he said
voice_notes.trap: two moments in one note; the fear level belongs to supper (s1), not to the pill (s2), which has no number

turns.text: Good afternoon, Jonah, and hello, Mrs. Abernathy. Thank you for all the entries this week. They're really thorough. Jonah, I'd like to start with you if that's okay. How's eating been?
Fine. Same.
Same as before. Your grandmother wrote about Sunday dinner with the pot roast. Can you tell me what was going on for you?
I just don't like big pieces anymore. If I cut it really small it's okay. And I drink water so it goes down.
What are you worried would happen with a bigger piece?
That it gets stuck. And I can't breathe. And nobody knows what to do.
Thanks for saying that. That's a scary thought to have every time you eat. If you think about sitting down to a dinner like the pot roast, zero to ten, how scared?
Eight, probably.
An eight. That's high. Mrs. Abernathy, what do you see at dinner?

I see him cutting everything into crumbs, really, and drinking water after each bite. And more and more he asks for soup or a smoothie instead of what I've cooked. I'm afraid I have been making it for him. I know you told us not to, but he's fourteen and growing, and I simply cannot watch him go to bed hungry.

That's a completely understandable feeling, and it comes from loving him. Making the soup does help tonight. What it also does is tell Jonah's worry that solid food really is dangerous. So next time, the worry is a little louder. We'll find a way through that doesn't leave him hungry.
Nana, where's the charger for the car?
In my purse, dear. Go on, we're in the middle of something.
No problem. Jonah, your grandmother also wrote about pizza at your friend's house.
Yeah. I had like two bites and my throat felt tight, like closing up. So I went to the bathroom. I didn't want them to see if something happened.
If something happened in front of your friends, what would that look like?
Like I start choking and somebody has to do the Heimlich on me and everyone's filming it.
That's a really clear picture. Thank you. We'll come back to eating with friends, I promise. The teacher also called your grandmother about lunch.
Yes, she said he sits with his friends but barely eats. Just pushes the food about. I honestly wasn't sure if it was the choking, or if something else is going on at school. I didn't want to assume.
Jonah, anything you want to add about lunch?
No. It's fine. I'm just not hungry at school.
Okay. I'll leave that there for today. Can we talk about the allergy pill?
I crush it into applesauce every morning. Have done since the summer.
Jonah, is the pill like the food, the same worry?
Kind of. It's hard and it doesn't chew. It could just sit there.

Got it. Here's what I'd like to try this week, and I want both of you to agree. We'll start with dinner at home, where it feels safest. Jonah, at dinner, three nights this week, you eat pieces of whatever Nana cooks that are bigger than you usually cut. Not huge. Maybe the size of your thumbnail. And you take a drink of water only every three or four bites, not after every one. Does that sound possible?
Thumbnail size. And not water every bite.
Right. And you rate your fear before dinner and after, zero to ten. Mrs. Abernathy, could you write those numbers in the app?
Yes, I can do that.

And the harder one for you. On those three nights, there's no separate soup or smoothie. Jonah eats what the family eats, at the size we agreed. If he eats less than usual, that's okay for a few nights. He won't come to harm from a smaller supper.
Three nights. No soup. Goodness. All right. I'll try.
You don't need to say anything about it at the table. Just serve dinner like normal. If he asks for soup, you can say 'not tonight, love, this is what we're having.'
What about the pill?
We're leaving the pill alone for now. Applesauce is fine this week. We'll make a separate plan for the pill later on. Just dinners for now.
Thank you. I was worried you'd want to stop the applesauce straight away.
Not yet. Jonah, can you tell me back what we agreed?
Three dinners. Thumbnail-size bites. Water every few bites, not every one. Rate it before and after. No soup those nights.
That's exactly it. Great job today, Jonah. That took courage to talk about. See you both next week.

The pill stays in applesauce this week

A Fear Level for eating with friends or for the pill (none was said in the session)
A referral for a swallowing study or other medical test
A conclusion that school lunch is caused by the choking fear (it was left open)
